paper_identity.title: Continuous Kasteleyn theory for the bead model
paper_identity.source_version_limit: No asserted byte or content equivalence with publisher edition.

summary: Theorem1.12 has a false probability-density normalization, contradicted by the admissible one-particle case; its proof gives the corrected constant. Theorem4.1 cannot hold over its unrestricted p=k/n range. Theorem5.2 also omits a local factor1/2 that cancels in normalized correlation ratios. Fixed-p Theorem1.4 and the main Kasteleyn construction are not refuted by these checks.

problems.title: Incorrect change-of-measure constant in Theorem1.12

claim.location: Theorem1.12,p9; definitions and ratespp8-9; generators(6.21)-(6.22)p45; proof(6.26)-(6.27)p46
claim.text: The probability Radon-Nikodym derivative uses c=n_particle-(1/n)sin(pi*l/n)/sin(pi/n).

assumptions: Both chains start from the same fixed configuration, as in the proof, or the same initial law.
Allowed jumps are h->h+1 into a vacancy; Gordenko ratesDelta(E')/Delta(E),TASEP rates1.
problems.check: Take ell1,anyn>=2:Delta=1,Traffic0,mu1. Both generators equalf(h+1)-f(h),so laws coincide and true density1. Printed densityexp[-(1-1/n)t] is deterministic below1 for t>0.
problems.result: The stated expression is not a unit-mean martingale or probability density.
counterevidence: Actual page images confirm the printed1/n and unscaled rates; not extraction error.
The proof itself gives generator identity(mu-ell+Traffic)Delta and correct constantell-mu.
The1/n legitimately measures per-string bead density, not total jump rate.
The correction is compatible with the one-particle case and every bounded finite generator diagnostic.
problems.impact: Material false normalization in a stated principal probability theorem; Major. No collapse of the determinant construction claimed.

correction.text: Use c=ell-sin(pi*ell/n)/sin(pi/n),with identical initial laws. Product of jump-rate ratios telescopesDelta(X0)/Delta(Xt),and holding-rate difference givesmu-ell+Traffic.

problems.title: Unrestricted uniform asymptotic parameter range

claim.location: Theorem4.1,(4.11),p23; final prefactor replacementp29; Corollary1.3,p5 and derivationpp22-23
claim.text: Uniform estimate with universal constants whenever n^-1/4<=tau<=1-n^-1/4 and p=k/n>=n^-1/4,without any upper bound onp.

assumptions: Evenn>=16,ell=n/2 gives tau1/2 within both stated bounds.
k is a positive integer chosen large enough that p=k/n exceeds the stated lower bound.
Exact root-sum coefficient identity and its parity/complement derivation retained.
problems.check: Consecutive half-root blocks contribute n M_n^(nk)/(nk)!,M_n=1/sin(pi/n); all other blocks have strict modulus ratio rho_n<1. Relative error bounded byB_n rho_n^(nk). Ratio to claimed exp(p*pi²/6)/sqrt(2*pi*p) equals(1+epsilon)exp[pA_n-r_N],A_n=n²log[(pi/n)/sin(pi/n)]-pi²/6>0. Choosek_n soerror<=1/n andpA_n>=n. Actualratio diverges; claimedpartitionbracket tends1.
problems.result: The unrestricted uniform range is false; the final sine approximation has logarithmic error beginningp/n².
counterevidence: Theorem1.4p5 fixesp andtau,so this obstruction does not refute its limit.
Complex cancellation in nonconsecutive root sums is bounded in absolute value; no assumption that all terms are positive.
Every parameter restriction is met by the diagonal integer family.
Numerical sine diagnostics are corroborating only; the contradiction is analytical.
problems.impact: False stronger fine-volume guarantee closely tied to advertised asymptotic result; Major within that stated range. No refutation of fixed-p free energy is claimed.

correction.text: Retain exact finite-n sine/factorial prefactor or supply justified parameter restrictions and quantitative remainders. This removes one lost factor, but no complete repaired uniform theorem is asserted.

checks.derivation: At ell=1, Delta=1, Traffic=0 and both explicitly unscaled generators have unit jump rates. Their laws with identical initial states/laws coincide; the printed exp[-(1-1/n)t] has mass below one. For general ell, the product of jump-rate ratios telescopes Delta(X0)/Delta(Xt), while the total holding-rate difference is mu-ell+Traffic. Source (6.26)-(6.27) confirms c=ell-mu, without 1/n.
checks.assessment: Major false principal normalization, with the source proof supplying the checked repair; per-string density is a distinct legitimate occurrence of 1/n.

checks.derivation: For even n>=16 and ell=n/2, projection onto the direction of a root sum shows that only consecutive half-root blocks maximize modulus M=1/sin(pi/n). Their N=nk powers have the same sign cancelled by the exact volume prefactor. Other terms are bounded by B_n rho_n^N with rho_n<1. Stirling gives the normalized ratio (1+epsilon) exp[p A_n-r_N], where A_n=n^2 log[(pi/n)/sin(pi/n)]-pi^2/6>0. Choosing integer k_n so the nonmaximal error<=1/n and p A_n>=n yields divergence under every stated lower-bound constraint, while the claimed partition bracket tends to 1.
checks.assessment: Major false stronger uniform guarantee. The fixed-p Theorem 1.4 obstruction vanishes; neither that limit nor a complete repaired uniform remainder is certified.

checks.derivation: For n=2,theta=(1,1),lambda=log2 and one occupied observation, beta=lambda+pi i gives C(w,w)=1/3, so the printed determinant side is (3/2)^2/3=3/4. Actual density (5.11) is (1/2)(1/2)(3/2)=3/8. It is an admissible nonempty determinant. Restoring 1/2 in both (5.29) and its normalization (5.30) leaves ratio (5.31) unchanged.
checks.assessment: Minor local normalization error; no false normalized correlation kernel established.
